claims: Most Kickstarter campaigns fail because they burn money before learning nobody wants the product (Google AI overview cites ~40-43% success)
Need: a contact data source + 'this prompt'; AI builds 3 audiences, ~10 Workspace mailboxes, a sequencer, variant emails per audience
Emails should look like you are forwarding a marketing email; then AI analyses opens/clicks, removes bot clicks, finds which audience likes which variant
'I did a version of this and it kind of worked'; actually talking to customers on Zoom was 'way more helpful'
how_to_steps: Ask Claude to find three work audiences for the product (demo: developers, designers, consultants for a portable monitor) using Apollo/Prospeo
Create ~10 Google Workspace mailboxes and connect them to an email sequencer (Smartlead)
Have Claude write marketing emails per audience showcasing different product versions (demo: portrait coding screen, dual-screen extender, color review monitor)
Build a tracking landing page first; link each offer to its send and log the follow-up button press
Have Claude filter scanner/robot clicks (rapid sweeps, control-link hits, timing/user-agent) and keep uncertain events separate
Compare qualified visits per audience/variant; retest winners against fresh contacts
on_screen_only: Google search 'why do most kickstarter campaigns fail' with AI Overview: 'Roughly 40% to 43%...'; Reddit r/kickstarter 'Most Kickstarter projects don't fail because of marketing. They fail long...'

Claude chat: 'Find three work audiences for this portable monitor. Show me a few sample fits.' -> 'Searching Apollo', 'Checking Prospeo' -> '1. Developers ... 2. Designers ... 3. Consultants ... Three demo profiles per audience for review. No outreach.'
Concept previews: Portrait coding screen (for developers), Dual-screen extender, Color review monitor (for designers), client display

Claude: 'Build the tracking page before we send anything.' -> 'Building landing page', 'Testing event collector', 'Seed test passed. offer_clicked -> solo, page_loaded -> session_0..., show_me_pressed -> sessio...', 'Events join... A page load alone does not count as a visit.'

Claude: 'Filter the robot clicks before you compare the audiences.' -> 'Control-link... scanner', 'Rapid... likely scanner', 'Separate... stronger signal', 'Uncertain events stay separate. No single rule catches every bot.'

'Which audience and version worked best after filtering?' -> 'Strongest candidate: deve... It had the highest observed qu... in this demo. The intervals overlap, so... winner yet. Next: retest B against A on fresh developers.'

Copyable prompt: 'Separate scanner activity 1. Read raw events joined to sends and assignments... write a classification with evidence: likely scanner, uncertain... 2. Flag control-link... sweeps as likely scanner... 3. Count a later, separate... press as stronger... 4. Deduplicate... the primary qualified-visit count...'
cta: follow; he open-sources his AI ideas for free

relevance.why: Cold-email demand testing is a grey-area tactic (spoofed 'forwarded' marketing emails from 10 burner mailboxes) and the creator himself says Zoom interviews were more useful; limited fit for Haji's apps

implement_score.why: The useful kernel is 'build a tracking landing page and filter bot clicks before trusting email metrics'. The 10-mailbox forwarded-email scheme risks domain reputation and CAN-SPAM issues; not recommended as is

verify: Legality/deliverability of sending unsolicited 'forwarded' marketing emails from burner Workspace accounts (CAN-SPAM, Google sending limits)
Apollo/Prospeo data costs and whether Claude connectors for them exist

gap.what: New technique (with caveats): pre-launch audience/variant demand test via sequencer emails plus a bot-click filtering prompt. Liked set covers PostHog archetype funnels and hook testing but not cold-email demand validation
